title: Orthogonal projection onto a graph plane via the Gram operator
statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, A : R^n -> R^l, J : R^n -> R^(n+l) and T : R^(n+l) -> R^n continuous linear maps such that J v = graphPoint v (A v) for every v in R^n and <T w, v> = <w, J v> for all w in R^(n+l), v in R^n. Then T o J is a unit of the ring L(R^n, R^n) of continuous linear endomorphisms (multiplication = composition), and the orthogonal projection (starProjection) of R^(n+l) onto Gamma_A = span{graphPoint v (A v) : v in R^n} equals J o (Ring.inverse(T o J) o T).
lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (A : Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ) (J : Rn n →L[ℝ] Amb n ℓ) (T : Amb n ℓ →L[ℝ] Rn n), (∀ v : Rn n, J v = graphPoint v (A v)) → (∀ (w : Amb n ℓ) (v : Rn n), inner ℝ (T w) v = inner ℝ w (J v)) → IsUnit (T ∘L J) ∧ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range fun v : Rn n => graphPoint v (A v))).starProjection = J ∘L Ring.inverse (T ∘L J) ∘L T
